native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (ever_jailed==1; n=289) had significantly lower wealth than those without (n=11,724) in every wealth year measured — 1985, 1990, and 1996 — confirmed by one-sided Mann-Whitney U tests (p=8.0e-11 / 3.9e-35 / 4.6e-26), all significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and Holm correction across the three year-tests, and robust to two-part decomposition, race/sex-adjusted IHS OLS, and deduplication. The largest rank gap was in 1990 (jailed median $0 vs not-jailed $10,500; Hodges-Lehmann shift $7,850; Cliff's delta -0.42), followed by 1996 (median $0 vs $8,500; delta -0.35) and 1985 (median $720 vs $3,600; delta -0.22).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Described groups and missingness (12,013x6, zero missing; 2.41% jailed). 2) One-sided Mann-Whitney U per year (jailed < not-jailed) on raw wealth; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR + Holm across the 3 year-tests (verified against statsmodels.multipletests). 3) Effect sizes: Hodges-Lehmann location shift, median difference with 4,000-iteration bootstrap 95% CI, mean difference, Cliff's delta/rank-biserial. 4) Robustness: two-part decomposition (chi2/Fisher on share wealth<=0; Welch t on log10 among positives), inverse-hyperbolic-sine covariate-adjusted OLS with race and sex, and BH-corrected tests after dropping full-row duplicates. 5) Reconciled raw vs corrected p-values and across all approaches: all three years significant everywhere; no analysis flips any conclusion. All results saved to artifacts/.

sub_hypo.text: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, with wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 (ever_jailed = 1) have significantly lower composite wealth in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996 than individuals not jailed during that period (ever_jailed = 0).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals ever jailed had significantly lower wealth in 1985, 1990, and 1996 than those not jailed, with the largest rank gap in 1990, followed by 1996 and 1985. This conclusion remained significant after multiple-testing corrections and robust across all reported sensitivity analyses.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort: 12,013 respondents with no missing values, including 289 ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 (2.41%) and 11,724 not jailed; wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Ever-jailed respondents had lower wealth in each year under one-sided Mann-Whitney U tests: p=8.0e-11 in 1985, 3.9e-35 in 1990, and 4.6e-26 in 1996, all significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and Holm correction across the three tests. Jailed versus not-jailed medians were $720 versus $3,600 in 1985 (Cliff's delta -0.22), $0 versus $10,500 in 1990 (delta -0.42; Hodges-Lehmann shift $7,850), and $0 versus $8,500 in 1996 (delta -0.35). Rank gaps were largest in 1990, then 1996, then 1985. Conclusions remained significant under two-part decomposition testing the share with wealth<=0 and log10 wealth among positive values, race/sex-adjusted inverse-hyperbolic-sine OLS, and BH-corrected tests after removing full-row duplicates.
